in_arabic.name: أنوشه

in_urdu.name: انوشہ
in_urdu.meaning: کوئی چھوٹی یا خوبصورت چیز، بہن یا بیٹی
in_urdu.long_meaning: انوشہ کا مطلب فارسی سے ماخوذ ہے اور اس کا معنی ہے کوئی چھوٹی یا خوبصورت چیز، بہن یا بیٹی۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافتوں میں خاص طور پر فارسی اور اردو بولنے والے ممالک میں مقبول ہے۔ اس کا تعلق فارسی زبان کے الفاظ سے ہے جو خوبصورتی یا چھوٹی اشیاء کو بیان کرتے ہیں

in_pashto.name: انوشه

historical_references.reference: Anusheh bint Rustom was a legendary figure in Persian history, the princess of the Sassanid Empire of Persia who converted to Islam during the early Islamic conquest of Persia. She is said to have fallen in love with Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab, and is famous for her exceptional beauty and intelligence. The exact time of her life is not known, but it is believed to be between the late 6th and early 7th centuries.

Anusheh bint Qais, also known as Anushtegin or Eanish, was a Persian noblewoman who played a significant role in the early Islamic history of Iran. She was the wife of Ali ibn Husayn, the fifth Shia Imam. She is renowned for her unwavering loyalty and support to Ali during his struggles against his political and military opponents, including the Umayyad Caliphate. Her story is often told as an example of the devotion and bravery of Shia women during this period. The time of her life is estimated to be between the mid-7th and early 8th centuries.
